items.title: [Performance]: gfx1100 ranks ROCM_ATTN above TRITON_ATTN for a custom kernel it does not use at head_size 256
items.body:
### Summary

On gfx1100 the ROCm selector has two eligible attention backends for this model and takes `ROCM_ATTN`, by the static priority order set in #36702. That order ranks `ROCM_ATTN` first for its custom paged-attention HIP kernel, but on RDNA that kernel is only instantiated at `head_size == 128`. On a `head_size` 256 model it is never called, both candidates run Triton kernels, and **the one the selector rejects is faster at decode at every depth measured** — 1.28x at 500 tokens rising to 10.74x at 32 K.

The obvious answer is that #45916 fixes `ROCM_ATTN`'s decode, and it does. The reason this is still worth reporting is that **the ranking question survives it**: with #45916 on `ROCM_ATTN` and #52684 on `TRITON_ATTN`, the selector's choice still costs 15.1 % of decode at 32 K and buys 4.4 % of prefill.

### Where the ranking premise fails

`ROCM_ATTN` does not call the HIP kernel directly. `rocm_attn.py` calls `chunked_prefill_paged_decode(...)`, which chooses:

```
chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py:373   use_custom = use_rocm_custom_paged_attention(...)
chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py:392   if use_custom:  ops.paged_attention_rocm(...)     # the HIP kernel
chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py:461   else:           kernel_paged_attention_2d[...]    # a Triton kernel
```

and the RDNA branch of that predicate (`rocm.py:410-422`) requires

```python
_ON_GFX1X and ... and head_size == 128 and block_size == 16
and (gqa_ratio >= 3 and gqa_ratio <= 16) and ...
```

At `head_size` 256 it is False, so `ROCM_ATTN` runs `kernel_paged_attention_2d` while `TRITON_ATTN` runs `unified_attention`. Two Triton kernels, and the selector prefers one of them for a property that neither has here.

That is recorded at runtime rather than read off the predicate. Both `ROCM_ATTN` arms log

```
WARNING [chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py:419] Cannot use ROCm custom paged
attention kernel, falling back to Triton implementation.
```

and the kernels their JIT monitor then reports compiling during inference are `kernel_paged_attention_2d` and, with #45916, `kernel_paged_attention_2d_splitkv{,_reduce}`. The two `TRITON_ATTN` arms carry neither line and compile `kernel_unified_attention` instead. The custom HIP kernel is never entered in any of the four arms.

`_get_backend_priorities` cannot express this: it takes `use_mla`, `use_sparse` and `use_kv_connector`, and never sees `head_size`. On gfx1100 AITER is unavailable, so the list is `['ROCM_ATTN', 'TRITON_ATTN']` and the order alone decides.

### Environment

```
2x AMD Radeon RX 7900 XT (gfx1100, RDNA3), TP=2, ROCm 10.0
vLLM 0.27.1.dev5+gf46a9dfe2.d20260827
model  Qwen3.8-27B-AWQ-INT4, from its own config.json: head_dim 256,
       num_attention_heads 24, num_key_value_heads 4 -> num_queries_per_kv = 6,
       64 layers = 48 linear_attention + 16 full_attention
serve  --max-model-len 33000 --max-num-seqs 16 --tensor-parallel-size 2
       --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 ; enable_prefix_caching=False
```

`vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_unified_attention.py` in this image is **byte-identical to `main`** (md5 `49fab3b643bf5a88eb65303ce377996b`, 1189 lines, zero differing lines against `5e71a11e`), so arms C and D below are measurements of main's own kernel and #52684 applies to it with no rejected hunks. `chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py` differs from main by 56 lines, all inside `kernel_paged_attention_2d`, where main skips the per-token load mask on non-final tiles. That is a speedup to exactly the kernel arm A runs, so **arm A understates main by an amount I have not measured**.

### The four arms

Same machine, same day, no service allowed back onto the cards between them. Within each pair the serve command is identical; what varies is which file is in site-packages, asserted by md5 before every arm.

| arm | `--attention-backend` | `triton_unified_attention.py` | `chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py` |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | *(none; selector picks ROCM_ATTN)* | image = main | image |
| B | *(none; selector picks ROCM_ATTN)* | image = main | + #45916 |
| C | `TRITON_ATTN` | image = main | + #45916 |
| D | `TRITON_ATTN` | + #52684 | + #45916 |

11 rungs from 500 to 32 000, two rounds each, grouped by target length. A rung is shown only when its two rounds agree within 8 %; cells are the mean of the two. 44 measurements per arm, 0 errors, decode 11/11 rungs on all four arms.

### Decode, tok/s

| ctx | A | B | C | D | C/A | D/B |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 500 | 38.45 | 49.62 | 49.23 | 49.33 | 1.28x | 0.994 |
| 2 000 | 27.01 | 48.88 | 48.75 | 48.86 | 1.81x | 0.999 |
| 4 000 | 19.30 | 47.84 | 48.22 | 48.28 | 2.50x | 1.009 |
| 8 000 | 12.38 | 45.82 | 47.25 | 47.28 | 3.82x | 1.032 |
| 16 000 | 7.17 | 42.18 | 45.27 | 45.37 | 6.31x | 1.076 |
| 24 000 | 5.06 | 39.16 | 43.51 | 43.58 | 8.60x | 1.113 |
| 32 000 | 3.90 | 36.43 | 41.91 | 41.95 | **10.74x** | **1.151** |

`C/A` is what the ranking costs on the image as it ships. `D/B` is what it still costs once both open PRs are in: the two are level to 4 000 and `TRITON_ATTN` pulls away after.

### Prefill, tok/s

| ctx | A | B | C | D | D/B |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 000 | 1029.1 | 952.7 | 970.3 | 983.2 | 1.032 |
| 4 000 | 1013.1 | 990.6 | 959.7 | 986.2 | 0.996 |
| 8 000 | 1013.5 | 1017.0 | 952.0 | 1016.8 | 1.000 |
| 16 000 | 1012.5 | 1015.5 | 862.6 | 1004.8 | 0.989 |
| 24 000 | 983.3 | 995.4 | 770.2 | 963.9 | 0.968 |
| 32 000 | 964.8 | 965.8 | 692.0 | 923.4 | **0.956** |

**Prefill is where `ROCM_ATTN` is genuinely ahead**, and this is the cost side of the report rather than the case for it. Fitting `t(n) = a + b*n + c*n²` over the chart-grade rungs, taking the faster round of each:

| arm | rungs | a ms | b µs/tok | c ns/tok² | r² |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A | 11/11 | 52.5 | 942.4 | **2.79** | 1.0000 |
| B | 10/11 | 219.6 | 919.8 | **3.23** | 0.9999 |
| C | 10/11 | 358.7 | 848.2 | **18.17** | 1.0000 |
| D | 10/11 | 260.8 | 886.0 | **5.84** | 1.0000 |

`TRITON_ATTN` is the better backend on the linear term throughout and pays for it on the quadratic one. #52684 takes that quadratic coefficient from 18.17 to 5.84 — at 32 K it removes 12.6 s of quadratic cost and adds 1.2 s of linear — which is what closes most of the prefill gap and leaves the 4.4 % above.

### What each open PR does to the comparison

**#45916** repairs `ROCM_ATTN`: decode at 32 K goes 3.90 to 36.43. It does not touch `TRITON_ATTN` (`triton_attn.py` calls `unified_attention`, not `chunked_prefill_paged_decode`), and it does not change `ROCM_ATTN`'s prefill.

**#52684** repairs `TRITON_ATTN`'s prefill: 692.0 to 923.4 at 32 K, with decode unchanged at every one of 11 rungs to within 0.25 %.

Neither settles the ranking. After both, `TRITON_ATTN` is 15.1 % ahead on decode at 32 K and 4.4 % behind on prefill, and the selector will still pick `ROCM_ATTN` every time.

### Proposed change

Make the RDNA ordering conditional on the thing that justifies it. When `use_rocm_custom_paged_attention` cannot be satisfied — on gfx1x, `head_size != 128` — demote `ROCM_ATTN` below `TRITON_ATTN` rather than excluding it, so it stays available as a fallback and CDNA is untouched. `get_valid_backends` already edits `backend_priorities` conditionally for the encoder-decoder case, with a TODO asking for exactly this kind of thing to be explicit in the selector, and `AttentionSelectorConfig` already carries `head_size`, so nothing needs plumbing:

```python
        if (
            on_gfx1x()
            and attn_selector_config.head_size != 128
            and AttentionBackendEnum.ROCM_ATTN in backend_priorities
            and AttentionBackendEnum.TRITON_ATTN in backend_priorities
        ):
            backend_priorities.remove(AttentionBackendEnum.ROCM_ATTN)
            backend_priorities.insert(
                backend_priorities.index(AttentionBackendEnum.TRITON_ATTN) + 1,
                AttentionBackendEnum.ROCM_ATTN,
            )
```

Filed as #54440, with two selector tests. The ordering was a deliberate decision in #36702, so the shape is genuinely open — in particular whether the condition should mirror the whole predicate (`block_size`, `gqa_ratio`, dtype, `kv_cache_dtype`) or only `head_size`, which is the part this data covers.

### What this claims, and what it does not

It claims: on gfx1100 at `head_size` 256, `ROCM_ATTN`'s custom kernel is not on the path; the selector prefers it anyway; and the preference is measurably wrong for decode both on the image as shipped and after both open PRs land.

It does not claim the ordering is wrong in general. CDNA is untested here, and `head_size` 128 — the case the ordering was tuned for — is left exactly as it is. It does not claim a prefill win: switching backends costs prefill, 1.39x on the release and 4.4 % after both PRs, and a prefill-dominated workload would prefer the current choice. One pass per arm, not order-reversed. And it does not measure upstream `main` with no patches at all, for the `kernel_paged_attention_2d` reason given above.

**On how far it generalises, the mechanism and the measurement are not the same claim.** The mechanism is a property of the predicate and holds for every affected model by construction: `use_rocm_custom_paged_attention`'s RDNA branch requires `head_size == 128`, so on gfx1x *any* model with a different head size gets `ROCM_ATTN`'s Triton fallback rather than its HIP kernel, and the reason `ROCM_ATTN` outranks `TRITON_ATTN` is void for all of them. That much is readable from the source and does not need a benchmark.

What is measured is **one model**: `Qwen3.8-27B-AWQ-INT4`, `head_dim` 256, 24 query heads over 4 KV heads. Whether the ranking actually inverts — whether `unified_attention` beats `kernel_paged_attention_2d` — depends on shape, and I have one shape. `head_size` 64 is disqualified by the same predicate and demoted by the same condition, with no data behind it at all.

The obvious second model would have been Gemma 4, which is also `head_dim` 256. It is not here for two reasons, both worth knowing: it cannot be served on this ROCm image at all (`AmbiguousGlobalPerLayerAttributeError` out of `model_arch_config_convertor.get_head_size`, fixed upstream in #49797 but not in this build), and where it does run, `Gemma4ModelConfig.verify_and_update_config` forces `TRITON_ATTN` for heterogeneous head dims — so it would never exercise the default ordering even if it loaded. A second measured shape needs a model I do not have.

### Raw data

Every round of every arm, the four serve logs, the md5 of each file state, and the scripts: https://github.com/cadamcat/dual-radeon-vllm/tree/main/benchmarks/gfx1100-backend-matrix-2026-08-30

items.title: [Bug]: structured output can sample unconstrained tokens when the draft hand-off goes stale (spec decode + async scheduling + PP)
items.body:
## Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ``` ```
## 🐛 Describe the bug ### Summary The draft-token hand-off from the worker to the scheduler carries no identity: `DraftTokensHandler` holds a single slot that every `execute_model` overwrites. When a structured-output request's drafts are lost that way, its `-1` placeholders survive into `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask`, which then writes `_full_mask` — **every token in the vocabulary allowed** — at rows that are real sampling positions. The worker verifies the genuine drafts from its own GPU-resident copy, so acceptance can walk straight into those rows and emit up to `num_speculative_tokens` tokens with no grammar constraint at all. The failure is silent by construction: the mask fails **open**. When the emitted tokens happen to be grammar-legal the request is quietly corrupted and keeps generating from a poisoned context; when they are not, the request dies with ``` ERROR [backend_xgrammar.py] Failed to advance FSM for request for tokens . ERROR [scheduler.py] Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [30, 128825, ...] for request . Terminating request. ``` **This is latent on `main` today** — see "Reachability" below. It becomes live the moment a pipeline-parallel-capable drafter lands, which is why it seems worth fixing before that happens rather than after. All line numbers below are `main` @ `87b9b5b`. ### The chain **1. The scheduler installs `-1` placeholders for the next step's drafts.** `vllm/v1/core/sched/async_scheduler.py:42-44` ```python # Add placeholders for the new draft/spec tokens. # We will update the actual spec token ids in the worker process. request.spec_token_ids = self._spec_token_placeholders # [-1] * K ``` **2. They are back-filled from a single, unidentified slot.** The deferred-sampling branch (`vllm/v1/engine/core.py:678`, back-fill at `:736`) calls `take_draft_token_ids()`, which resolves to `DraftTokensHandler` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/utils.py:11`): ```python def set_draft_tokens(self, input_batch, draft_tokens) -> None: self.req_ids = input_batch.req_ids # :25 — overwritten every step self.num_draft_tokens = draft_tokens.shape[1] if not input_batch.has_structured_output_reqs: self.draft_tokens_np = None # and cleared by plain batches return ``` No step id, no batch id, no history. The slot is correct only when the batch that last reached the worker covers the same requests as the step being sampled. That holds at `pipeline_parallel_size == 1`, where `max_concurrent_batches` is 2 (`vllm/config/vllm.py:563`): the deferred branch pops one entry and blocks on it, and the slot ends up holding exactly the predecessor's drafts. Under pipeline parallelism it does not hold. `max_concurrent_batches` becomes `pp_size + 1`, and `next_decode_eligible_step = current_step + pp_size` (`async_scheduler.py:48`) alternates requests across microbatches, so the batch that wrote the slot is a *different request set* than the one being sampled. There is also a second, more direct path (`utils.py:48-51`): ```python else: # This case only happens when async scheduling is disabled. draft_token_ids = [[-1] * self.num_draft_tokens for _ in self.req_ids] ``` That comment is not accurate: the branch is taken whenever the last batch to reach `set_draft_tokens` had no structured-output requests, which a plain-only microbatch does routinely. **3. A surviving `-1` makes the bitmask fail open.** `vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py:301-306` ```python for i, token in enumerate(req_tokens): self._fill_bitmasks(((grammar, cumulative_index, apply_bitmask),)) # row i filled FIRST advance_grammar = apply_bitmask if token == -1: # :304 apply_bitmask = False # rows i+1.. get _full_mask advance_grammar = False ``` `_full_mask` is `torch.tensor(-1, dtype=torch.int32)` — 32 bits set (`:59`, applied at `:213`) — and `apply_grammar_bitmask` only writes `-inf` where a bit is **0**. "The mask could not be built" therefore renders as "every token is allowed". Note that row 0 is filled *before* `req_tokens[0]` is inspected, so it is always correct. Only rows `1..K-1` go permissive. **4. Meanwhile the model verifies the real drafts, not the `-1`s.** The `-1` exists only in the scheduler's copy. The worker builds `input_ids` from its own GPU-resident `req_states.draft_tokens` via `combine_sampled_and_draft_tokens`, so the rejection sampler verifies genuine draft tokens against rows whose mask allows everything. Accepting any of them emits a token the grammar never allowed. ### Reproduction on stock `main`, without a model `repro.py` below drives the two links directly. It needs a CUDA device (for the handler's copy stream) and the `gpt2` tokenizer; no model weights.
repro.py ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Reproduce the structured-output hole on stock vLLM main, without a model. The end-to-end symptom needs pipeline parallelism, and every draft head whose checkpoint is small enough to test with (Eagle3Llama, MiMoMTP, ...) refuses PP because it does not implement `SupportsPP`, while `create_draft_parallel_config` copies the target's pp_size verbatim. So drive the two links of the chain directly instead; together they are the whole bug. Link A `DraftTokensHandler` keeps ONE slot with no identity, so a batch that does not contain a request destroys that request's drafts. Link B the `-1` placeholders that therefore survive make `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask` emit `_full_mask` -- every token allowed -- at rows that are REAL sampling positions, because the worker verifies the genuine drafts from its own GPU-resident copy. Run with the stock venv: .venv/bin/python stock_unit_repro.py """ import sys from types import SimpleNamespace import numpy as np import torch from transformers import AutoTokenizer from vllm.config import StructuredOutputsConfig, VllmConfig from vllm.config.model import ModelConfig from vllm.config.speculative import SpeculativeConfig from vllm.sampling_params import SamplingParams, StructuredOutputsParams from vllm.v1.request import Request from vllm.v1.structured_output import StructuredOutputManager from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.utils import DraftTokensHandler TOKENIZER = "gpt2" K = 4 ok = True def report(name, holds, detail=""): """Each assertion states an observed fact about the current code. `yes` means the fact holds, which for the Link A/B facts means the bug is present.""" global ok ok = ok and holds print(f" [{'yes' if holds else 'NO '}] {name}{(' ' + detail) if detail else ''}") # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Link A: the single slot has no identity. # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- def link_a(): print("\nLink A -- DraftTokensHandler keeps one unidentified slot") dev = torch.device("cuda:0") handler = DraftTokensHandler(dev) # Only `req_ids` and `has_structured_output_reqs` are read off the batch. def batch(req_ids, structured): return SimpleNamespace( req_ids=list(req_ids), has_structured_output_reqs=structured ) drafts_a = torch.arange(1, 1 + 2 * K, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev).reshape(2, K) drafts_b = torch.arange(101, 101 + 2 * K, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev).reshape(2, K) # Batch A carries the structured-output request. handler.set_draft_tokens(batch(["gA", "pA"], True), drafts_a) got = handler.get_draft_tokens() report( "drafts for 'gA' are available right after its own batch", "gA" in got.req_ids, f"req_ids={got.req_ids}", ) # Another microbatch runs. Under PP this is the other half of the requests. handler.set_draft_tokens(batch(["gB", "pB"], True), drafts_b) got = handler.get_draft_tokens() report( "after another batch runs, 'gA' can no longer be found", "gA" not in got.req_ids, f"req_ids={got.req_ids} -- gA's drafts are gone, with nothing recording that", ) # A batch with no structured-output request clears the payload entirely and # still overwrites req_ids. get_draft_tokens then returns all -1 for a set of # requests it was never asked about. handler.set_draft_tokens(batch(["p1", "p2"], False), drafts_b) got = handler.get_draft_tokens() all_minus_one = all(all(t == -1 for t in row) for row in got.draft_token_ids) report( "a plain-only batch makes get_draft_tokens return all -1", all_minus_one, f"req_ids={got.req_ids} drafts={got.draft_token_ids}", ) print( " (utils.py comment claims this 'only happens when async " "scheduling is disabled')" ) # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Link B: a surviving -1 turns the mask fully permissive at real positions. # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- def link_b(): print("\nLink B -- surviving -1 makes grammar_bitmask fail OPEN") tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(TOKENIZER) vllm_config = VllmConfig( model_config=ModelConfig(tokenizer=TOKENIZER), structured_outputs_config=StructuredOutputsConfig(backend="xgrammar"), speculative_config=SpeculativeConfig( model="[ngram]", num_speculative_tokens=K ), ) manager = StructuredOutputManager(vllm_config) sampling_params = SamplingParams( structured_outputs=StructuredOutputsParams(json='{"type": "object"}') ) sampling_params.structured_outputs._backend = "xgrammar" sampling_params.update_from_generation_config({}, tokenizer.eos_token_id) prompt = tokenizer.encode('{"a"') request = Request( "req", prompt_token_ids=prompt, sampling_params=sampling_params, pooling_params=None, ) manager.grammar_init(request) while not request.structured_output_request._check_grammar_completion(): pass grammar = request.structured_output_request.grammar assert grammar.accept_tokens(request.request_id, prompt) # This is what the scheduler holds when the back-fill missed: the whole # window is still placeholders. window = [-1] * K bitmask = manager.grammar_bitmask( requests={request.request_id: request}, structured_output_request_ids=[request.request_id], scheduled_spec_decode_tokens={request.request_id: window}, ) assert bitmask is not None and bitmask.shape[0] == K + 1 row0_constrained = not (bitmask[0] == -1).all() report("row 0 is constrained (filled before the -1 is inspected)", row0_constrained) permissive = [i for i in range(1, K) if (bitmask[i] == -1).all()] report( "rows 1..K-1 are fully permissive", permissive == list(range(1, K)), f"rows {permissive} allow every token in the vocabulary", ) # And those rows are real sampling positions: the worker verifies the drafts # from its own GPU copy, so acceptance can walk into them. vocab = tokenizer.vocab_size row = bitmask[1] allowed = int(np.unpackbits(row.view(np.uint8), bitorder="little")[:vocab].sum()) report( "a permissive row allows the entire vocabulary", allowed == vocab, f"{allowed}/{vocab} token ids allowed at a position the model will sample", ) # Contrast: a fully back-filled window keeps every row constrained. Pick the # drafts from the grammar itself -- `validate_tokens` reports the accepted # prefix without advancing -- so this cannot fail on hand-picked token ids # that simply are not legal here. grammar.reset() assert grammar.accept_tokens(request.request_id, prompt) candidate = tokenizer.encode(':"b"')[:K] real = grammar.validate_tokens(list(candidate)) if not real: report("contrast: could not build a legal draft window", False, str(candidate)) else: bitmask2 = manager.grammar_bitmask( requests={request.request_id: request}, structured_output_request_ids=[request.request_id], scheduled_spec_decode_tokens={request.request_id: real}, ) any_permissive = [ i for i in range(bitmask2.shape[0]) if (bitmask2[i] == -1).all() ] report( "with real drafts, no row is permissive", not any_permissive, f"window of {len(real)} real drafts, permissive rows: {any_permissive}", ) def main(): print(f"vLLM under test: {__import__('vllm').__version__}") link_a() link_b() print() if ok: print("BUG REPRODUCED on stock main: the draft hand-off carries no") print("identity, so a request loses its drafts silently, and the grammar") print("bitmask then fails OPEN at real sampling positions.") return 1 print("at least one link no longer holds -- bug not reproduced here") return 0 if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main()) ```
Output on `main` @ `87b9b5b`: ``` vLLM under test: 0.28.1rc1.dev118+g87b9b5b8d Link A -- DraftTokensHandler keeps one unidentified slot [yes] drafts for 'gA' are available right after its own batch req_ids=['gA', 'pA'] [yes] after another batch runs, 'gA' can no longer be found req_ids=['gB', 'pB'] -- gA's drafts are gone, with nothing recording that [yes] a plain-only batch makes get_draft_tokens return all -1 req_ids=['p1', 'p2'] drafts=[[-1, -1, -1, -1], [-1, -1, -1, -1]] (utils.py comment claims this 'only happens when async scheduling is disabled') Link B -- surviving -1 makes grammar_bitmask fail OPEN [yes] row 0 is constrained (filled before the -1 is inspected) [yes] rows 1..K-1 are fully permissive rows [1, 2, 3] allow every token in the vocabulary [yes] a permissive row allows the entire vocabulary 50257/50257 token ids allowed at a position the model will sample [yes] with real drafts, no row is permissive window of 3 real drafts, permissive rows: [] BUG REPRODUCED on stock main: the draft hand-off carries no identity, so a request loses its drafts silently, and the grammar bitmask then fails OPEN at real sampling positions. ``` ### Reachability: why this is latent upstream today The end-to-end symptom needs `pipeline_parallel_size >= 2`, and that is currently unreachable for any small public checkpoint: - `create_draft_parallel_config` copies the target's pp_size to the drafter verbatim (`vllm/config/speculative.py:1647`), and `verify_with_parallel_config` then rejects any drafter that does not implement `SupportsPP`. - Of the registered draft heads, only `Glm4MoeLiteMTP` and `BailingMoeV3MTPModel` implement it. `Eagle3LlamaForCausalLM`, `MiMoMTP`, `DeepSeekMTP` and `DeepSeekV4MTP` do not. - Relaxing that gate is not sufficient either: with the check bypassed, `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` + `RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-speculator.eagle3` at `pp=2` fails while *constructing* the drafter on a non-last rank (`llama_eagle3.py:166` → `llama.py:282`). We hit the symptom in production because our deployment carries a local relaxation for a side-model drafter (a DSpark head, which runs on the last stage rather than being partitioned across stages) plus the PP plumbing to broadcast draft tokens between stages. Any upstream change that makes a side-model drafter work under PP — which seems a natural thing to want — turns this from latent into live. ### Field evidence (from that deployment) 2 nodes x 2 GPUs, `pipeline_parallel_size=2`, `tensor_parallel_size=2`, DeepSeek-V4-Flash with `dspark` K=7, xgrammar backend. | probe | result | |---|---| | `tool_choice=required`, solo into an idle engine | passes 3/3 | | `tool_choice=required`, one other grammar request decoding | **fails 3/3** | | `json_schema` | **fails** | | `tool_choice=auto`, `json_object`, plain text | passes (permissive grammar hides it) | | `temperature=0` | passes (the resample kernel returns early on the masked argmax) | | speculative decoding disabled | passes | Permissive grammars pass because an unconstrained token is usually still legal, which is why this presents for a long time as "one agent out of six occasionally emits garbage" rather than as a hard error. Instrumenting `update_draft_token_ids_in_output` to classify each structured-output request in the deferred `SchedulerOutput` (6 concurrent `tool_choice=required` requests, 2400+ deferred steps): ``` MISSING (absent from draft_token_ids.req_ids) 100% ALL_MINUS1 (present, all drafts -1) 0% REAL ~0% ``` Retaining the last 4 snapshots and reporting at what depth the request's drafts would have been found: ``` MISSING@depth1 == MISSING 100% ``` The drafts are never actually unavailable — they are exactly one snapshot away, 100% of the time, which is the signature of a single slot under alternating PP microbatches. Solo, the back-fill succeeds ~85% of the time, which is why this only shows up under concurrency. Histogram of where the first `-1` lands in the K=7 window, same load: ``` first -1 at index -> {0: 2710, 1: 6, 2: 4, 3: 3, 4: 4, 5: 21, 6: 12, 7: 1309} ``` 66% of grammar rows had no usable draft at all, i.e. rows 1..7 permissive. ### Relationship to #44006 #44006 made the **bonus** row stay constrained after `-1` padding, and `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py:144` asserts exactly that: ```python assert not (bitmask[-1] == -1).all() ``` Rows `1..K-1` are deliberately left permissive, on the assumption that a `-1` means "this draft was rejected by `validate_tokens`, so the sampler will reject it too". That assumption is sound when the `-1` really is a rejection signal. It is violated here, where `-1` means "the drafts never reached the scheduler" — and no test covers those rows. `rejection_sampler_utils.py:767` already resamples a `-1` position straight from the target distribution and needs no change. ### Suggested fix Two independent pieces; the first is the correctness fix and stands alone. 1. **Fail closed.** When a structured-output request's scheduled spec tokens still contain `-1` at index `j`, mark drafts `j..K-1` invalid (`is_valid_draft = draft_sampled >= 0`) so the accepted length cannot run past the last row with a real mask. Rows `0..j` are correctly masked, so row `j` still supplies the step's token under the right constraint. Cost: that step gets no speculative speed-up. 2. **Give the hand-off an identity.** Snapshot `req_states.draft_tokens` where `prepare_inputs` feeds it into `input_ids` — at *consumption* time, not proposal time — tagged with the scheduler's step counter, and retain the last few. The scheduler then asks for the snapshot belonging to the step it is sampling, by equality, instead of taking whatever ran last. A miss falls back to (1), so the failure mode is the conservative one rather than a wrong mask. Both are implemented and running in our deployment. Measured effect of (2) on top of (1), 5 concurrent requests, aggregate decode throughput: | grammar + plain | (1) only | (1)+(2) | |---|---|---| | 1 + 4 | 235.6 | 256.0 | | 3 + 2 | 170.7 | 260.2 | | 5 + 0 | 111.9 | **276.8** | With (2), grammar requests decode at 52–58 tok/s against a 52.5 tok/s plain-text baseline — the speculative speed-up is fully recovered. Back-fill hit rate goes to 100%, and bitmask rows carrying a real mask from 32% to 96.5%. Happy to open PRs for both if this looks like the right direction. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Searched existing issues and asked the documentation chatbot.

items.title: [Bug] hy_v4 (Hy4-preview): degenerate output with FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120 — the only available sparse backend on SM120
items.body:
**Summary**: On RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120, CC 12.0), serving Hy4-preview (`hy_v4`, merged in #54160) produces degenerate output (`" of of of of…"` at temperature 0 from any prompt, including 5-token prompts) when using `--attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120`. This is the only selectable sparse-MLA backend on SM120: the prescribed `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` gates to `major in [9, 10]`, and hy_v4 sparse layers correctly refuse dense fallback.

**Setup**: 2 nodes × 4× RTX PRO 6000 Max-Q 96 GB, TP8 over Ray, image `vllm/vllm-openai:hy4-preview` (+ ray), driver 595.71.05. Weights: an experts-only NVFP4 cast of the official MXFP8 checkpoint (produced locally to fit 768 GB VRAM; expert tensors validated against `nvfp4_emulation_utils.dequantize_to_dtype`, 0.094 rel err vs the MXFP8 reference). Server reaches HEALTHY at `--max-model-len 530000`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`.

**Elimination evidence** (all A/B on the same live cluster, identical degenerate output in every case):
- MoE expert backends ×3: `flashinfer_cutlass`, `marlin`, `emulation` — byte-identical output, so expert kernels/quant path exonerated.
- MXFP8 linear kernels ×2: `FlashInferCutlassMxfp8LinearKernel` and (via `VLLM_DISABLED_KERNELS`) `MarlinMxfp8LinearKernel` — identical.
- Model-side code verified consistent with Tencent's reference implementation: elementwise sigmoid gate applied to decompressed attn_out; `is_neox_style=False`; sink params dumped from the checkpoint are modest (per-layer means 0.1–0.7, max 3.2), so the backend's warned sink-disable should be mild, not catastrophic.
- 5-token prompt repro ⇒ indexer *scoring* exonerated (top-k ⊇ all tokens).
- The backend rejects `bfloat16` KV (`kv_cache_dtype not supported`), so fp8-KV numerics cannot be ruled out by dtype A/B — fp8-class KV is mandatory on this path.

**Remaining suspects, in the backend**: fp8_ds_mla KV numerics on SM120, and/or the sparse kernel's handling of hy_v4's *gated* DSA / IndexCache (this backend was validated for DeepSeek/GLM shapes; hy_v4 is its first gated-MLA consumer). Possibly a FlashInfer-side issue — happy to re-file there if triage points that way.

**Ask**: (a) is hy_v4 × FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120 expected to work, or should SM120 be documented as unsupported for hy_v4? (b) If expected: full logs and configs available on request.

items.title: [RFC] Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: fp8_e4m3 KV cache on the QSA path — working patch, one machine, looking for corroboration
items.body:
## TL;DR

The QSA path of `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` refuses any KV dtype other than bf16. Most of
the machinery for fp8 is already in vLLM — only the **read** side of the QSA Triton
kernels was missing. Wiring it up roughly doubles the KV pool.

Measured on **one** GB10 (DGX Spark, sm_121):

| | bf16 | fp8_e4m3 | |
|---|---|---|---|
| KV pool | 780 638 tokens | **1 399 848** | ×1.79 |
| Max concurrency @ 262144 tok/req | 2.98× | **5.34×** | +79 % |
| Needle-in-a-haystack, 5 depths | — | **5/5** | |
| Decode, single stream, 100k ctx | — | 32.0 tok/s | no regression |

A working diff is here: https://gist.github.com/Nanetnounou/2e6486dd033bf077a9b8fdfcb6e1f7c8 (against vLLM `0.1.dev20073+g8e685d198`). **This is not a merge request yet** — see *What is not
tested* below. Posting it as an RFC because the interesting part may be the four
non-obvious integration points, and because a single machine is thin evidence.

## The problem

On a single 128 GB unified-memory box this model is attractive, but the KV pool
binds: at 262144 tokens per request the engine sustains ~3 concurrent requests, so
admission closes as soon as a queue forms — the normal regime under load, not an
incident.

`--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` fails with:

```
NotImplementedError: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next QSA requires a BF16 main KV cache
```

## What already worked

The change is small because most of it exists already:

| Piece | Before |
|---|---|
| `get_kv_cache_spec` passes `kv_quant_mode` | wired |
| `_k_scale` / `_v_scale` registered | wired |
| Quantised allocation | core |
| KV **write** via `reshape_and_cache_flash` | dtype-aware |
| KV **read** in QSA Triton kernels | **missing** |

The guards were doing the right thing: refusing rather than reading incorrectly.

## The four things that were not obvious

Sharing these because they are what cost the time, and none is visible from
reading the QSA sources alone.

1. **The cache is allocated as `uint8`**, not `float8_e4m3fn`. It needs
   `.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn)` before the kernel — exactly what `triton_attn.py`
   already does for unified attention. Without it, the kernel converts the
   *integer* rather than decoding the float.

2. **The block selector reads a different cache.** `qsa_mqa_paged` operates on the
   indexer's `raw_key_cache`, a separate tensor that follows the same dtype.
   Reinterpreting only the main cache left the selector reading bytes as floats,
   so it picked essentially arbitrary blocks. Outputs then diverged **from the
   first token** while the decode path was correct and the engine looked healthy.
   This was by far the hardest to find.

3. **Shared memory.** `_cast_kv_tile` materialises an fp32 tile, doubling shared
   memory for K and V. The kernel requested 106496 bytes against sm_121's 101376
   and failed to start. Halving `block_n` under quantisation fits.

4. **A guard inherited from `FlashAttentionImpl`** rejects a quantised cache
   because *its* kernels cannot read it on this device. QSA does not use them — it
   calls `qsa_sparse_paged_attention` in Triton and only inherits the surrounding
   plumbing.

## What the patch does

Reuses `_cast_kv_tile` from `triton_unified_attention.py` in both QSA kernels
rather than writing a second dequantisation; reinterprets `uint8` for both the
main and the indexer cache; halves `block_n` under quantisation; relaxes the
dtype guards. Inert in bf16 — `KV_QUANT_MODE` is a `constexpr`, so the branch is
compiled out.

89 added / 12 removed, across two files — [diff](https://gist.github.com/Nanetnounou/2e6486dd033bf077a9b8fdfcb6e1f7c8).

## On throughput — we do not claim a win

At typical context lengths the KV is a small fraction of the bytes read per token
compared with the active weights (this is an MoE: 6 B active of 176 B), so halving
it saves roughly 1–4 %. Decode measured 34.4 / 35.1 / 32.0 tok/s at 4k / 32k /
100k context: flat. The gain is **capacity**, not speed, and the numbers are given
to show absence of regression only.

## What is NOT tested

Being explicit, because this is the weak part:

- **One machine, one architecture** (sm_121). The AMD QSA owner carries the same
  guards and was left untouched.
- **No long-run soak.** On this same model a prefix-caching bug once booted fine,
  served ~105k reused tokens, then died on an illegal memory access. Twenty
  minutes of tests say nothing about two hours.
- **bf16 no-op not verified on a live engine** — only on synthetic tensors. The
  claim that the patch is inert in bf16 is reasoned, not measured end to end.
- **Prefix-cache hit vs miss not compared** under fp8.
- **fp8_e4m3 only**, per-tensor scales only. nvfp4 would be separate work: there is
  no Triton dequantisation to reuse for it in-tree (the only NVFP4 KV path is in
  the FlashInfer backend), and it needs 4-bit unpacking with nested fp8 scales.

Those tests are being run; results will be posted here. If the patch is useful,
they should land before any merge request.

## What would help

- Anyone with a second sm_121 box: does the pool roughly double for you too?
- Anyone on other hardware: does the guard removal hold, or does something else
  break first?
- Maintainers: is reusing `_cast_kv_tile` across model-specific kernels the
  intended direction, or is a QSA-local helper preferred?

## Prior art

The same idea was implemented independently for SGLang on a two-node setup, which
was a useful signal that a quantised KV is viable on this architecture at all.
That work upcasts K/V to fp32 in-kernel; this patch keeps vLLM's own convention
(`_cast_kv_tile` scales in fp32 and returns at the query dtype) so the QSA path
stays aligned with the rest of the tree.

items.title: [Bug]: V2 sampler warmup misses explicit-seed native path when FlashInfer is enabled
items.body:
### Your current environment

Field deployment:

- 4× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs (97,887 MiB each)
- NVIDIA driver 595.58.03, CUDA 13.2
- TP4 / DCP4, V2 model runner, FlashInfer sampler enabled
- Full GLM-5.3 checkpoint on a downstream vLLM/B12X image

The fatal field reproduction was on a downstream build, not stock vLLM `main`. I am filing this upstream because the same dispatch invariant is present in upstream commit [`5e71a11e`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/5e71a11eb2b595ede15ecc39c7dddca38e03deb5).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

V2 sampler warmup does not exercise the native sampling path selected by an explicit per-request seed when FlashInfer is enabled. Consequently, the engine can become ready before native top-k/top-p and Gumbel kernels have compiled or made their first temporary allocations. The first seeded API request can then JIT/allocate a materially different path and OOM under tight residual headroom.

The source path at `5e71a11e` is deterministic:

1. [`SamplingParams.for_sampler_warmup()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5e71a11eb2b595ede15ecc39c7dddca38e03deb5/vllm/sampling_params.py#L1234-L1253) says it exercises all sampler logic, but supplies no `seed`.
2. [`warmup_kernels()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5e71a11eb2b595ede15ecc39c7dddca38e03deb5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/warmup.py#L257-L283) assigns that unseeded configuration to all warmup requests.
3. The V2 sampler [disables FlashInfer when `any_explicit_seed()` is true](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5e71a11eb2b595ede15ecc39c7dddca38e03deb5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/sampler.py#L284-L320). With no seed, warmup takes FlashInfer; a seeded request takes native top-k/top-p plus Gumbel.
4. Although current warmup includes a one-request decode step, it remains unseeded. If the native path were selected, a batch below eight rows would [use the PyTorch full-vocabulary sort path](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5e71a11eb2b595ede15ecc39c7dddca38e03deb5/vllm/v1/sample/ops/topk_topp_sampler.py#L352-L388), another path not covered by the unseeded one-request warmup.

A mixed seeded/unseeded warmup batch would not cover both backends: `any_explicit_seed()` disables FlashInfer for the whole sampled batch.

### Reproduction and field evidence

A source-level reproduction does not require an OOM:

1. Enable the V2 model runner and FlashInfer sampling.
2. Instrument `flashinfer_sample`, `apply_top_k_top_p`, and `gumbel_sample`.
3. Run engine warmup. Only the unseeded FlashInfer path is selected.
4. Send a one-request stochastic completion with an explicit `seed`. Native top-k/top-p and Gumbel are selected for the first time after readiness.

The memory impact was observed on a near-capacity field deployment:

- A fixed 4,518,907,904-byte KV allocation per GPU passed deterministic startup and a 32K retrieval gate.
- The first `temperature=1` request with an explicit seed, 1,027 API prompt tokens, and 512 requested output tokens OOMed in top-p sampling and left workers hung with only 3–169 MiB physically free per rank.
- Reducing fixed KV to 3,415,867,392 bytes per GPU returned approximately 1.027 GiB/rank. The same seeded first-use path and subsequent C8 workload passed.
- On an exact-image control, `_gumbel_sample_kernel` first JIT-compiled after API application startup, directly showing that engine warmup had not exercised the runtime path.

The rejected arm's raw fatal trace was not retained, so I cannot make a more specific claim about the final failed allocation size. The request shape, top-p location, post-ready native-path selection, worker hang, and per-rank physical-memory minima were retained. Full field accounting and caveats are recorded [here](https://github.com/malaiwah/glm52-exl3-vast/blob/e0a84f9be9781618db0879d17e986c5a63897eb7/TEST_RESULTS.md#L208-L341).

### Expected behavior

Before reporting readiness, warmup should exercise both supported backend classes that may JIT or allocate differently:

- unseeded FlashInfer sampling;
- explicitly seeded native top-k/top-p plus Gumbel sampling, including a one-request/small-row shape.

### Suggested fix

Run separate sampler warmup passes for the unseeded and explicitly seeded configurations. Preserve the existing one-request decode shape for the seeded pass so the small-row native implementation is covered. A regression test could instrument backend dispatch and assert that FlashInfer, native top-k/top-p, and Gumbel have all run before warmup returns.

Related but not duplicate reports: #23322, #30637, and #33920 cover sampler/KV memory or full-vocabulary-sort OOMs, but not the seed-dependent FlashInfer/native dispatch gap.

### Before submitting a new issue

- [x] I searched existing issues for `for_sampler_warmup`, `any_explicit_seed`, seeded sampler warmup, FlashInfer, and Gumbel warmup.
- [x] I checked the behavior against current upstream source rather than assuming the downstream field build matched upstream.

items.title: [Bug][Feature][KV-offloading]: shared-mmap CPU region assumes all ranks on one host — multi-node engines hang at init; node-local disk tier reference implementation
items.body:
### Bug half

`SharedOffloadRegion` is one mmap file with a slot per rank. On a multi-node engine (mp executor with `--nnodes 2`, ranks on different hosts) the remote rank's slot is never written and startup dies after a multi-minute opaque wait:

```
TimeoutError: Timed out waiting for mmap file to reach 4144029696 bytes
```

`TieringOffloadingSpec` cannot avoid it: it overrides `_uses_shared_region → True` because the scheduler-side StoreController pushes L1 bytes to secondary tiers through a whole-region memoryview — single-host by construction. Plain `CPUOffloadingSpec` could fall back to private pinned tensors (which work fine multi-node), but has no gate either.

**Suggested minimal fix:** detect ranks-per-host at spec init and fail fast with an explicit "multi-node engines are not supported by the shared-region CPU tier" (or fall back to private tensors for the non-tiering spec). Related lifecycle work: #51317 / #52596 (leaked/unlinked regions — we added supporting evidence there from unified-memory hardware, where leaked regions silently shrink the next boot's profiled memory).

### Feature half: node-local tier for multi-node engines

For multi-node engines we built a working alternative worth considering in-tree: a spec where the scheduler keeps **metadata only** (persistent key index; per-key file paths derived from block hashes) and **each rank performs its own disk I/O against node-local storage** — shards never cross nodes and are never duplicated. ~450 lines over `CPUOffloadingSpec`, loaded via the existing `spec_module_path` hook, no core changes beyond the per-group geometry in #54413.

Production numbers (2× NVIDIA DGX Spark, GB10 unified memory, GLM-5.3-Flash EXL3 TP=2 with DFlash2 speculation): 155k-token session restored in 36.6 s vs 205 s recompute after a **full engine restart**; 10 *simultaneous* restores after restart, 10/10 needle-correct, TTFTs 18–164 s stacking gracefully.

Code: https://gist.github.com/hughmadden/03f369339b709a80fd594f4083702722

Hardening findings that generalize to any persistent tier (details in the gist):

- `PYTHONHASHSEED` must be pinned or block-hash-derived filenames change every restart → silent 0% hit rate (the fs manager documents this for cross-*process* sharing; it equally applies across restarts of one instance).
- Store completion must be decoupled from persistence (snapshot the bytes, complete the job, drain writes from private copies with a bounded backpressure queue) — otherwise long prefills stall on the block-reuse fence and the engine dies with `TimeoutError: RPC call to sample_tokens timed out`.
- Capacity-gated lookups race prepare-time allocation across requests within one scheduling step; a per-step committed-capacity counter (reset in `on_schedule_end`) closes it. Possibly relevant to #54363's I/O-liveness discussion.

Happy to contribute any of this as PRs if there's maintainer appetite.

items.title: [Feature][KV-offloading]: recent-window state groups can never participate in restores — per-group offload exclusion + hit-boundary rollback (GLM-5.3 tail_cache)
items.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Some hybrid-model KV groups hold *recent-window state* rather than restorable prefix state. GLM-5.3-Flash's 4-token DSA-indexer `tail_cache` keeps only a live window, which breaks the OffloadingConnector three independent ways:

1. Its engine-side block table is much shorter than `cdiv(hit_tokens, block_size)`, so `update_state_after_alloc` dies on `assert len(group_blocks) >= num_gpu_blocks` for any external hit that includes the group.
2. SWA-style store selection always lands on null placeholder blocks — the group can never store a chunk.
3. Any lookup chain that includes it collapses the min-across-groups hit window to zero — so one such group makes the **whole model** un-restorable even when every other group's chunks are stored and hit.

Related: #52771 / #52735 diagnose the adjacent all-groups-drafter-fallback defect under MTP/EAGLE (which we also hit); this issue is about groups that are *architecturally* unrestorable rather than volatile-tail handling.

### Proposed change (running in production)

Three cooperating hooks (config-driven in our deployment, `kv_connector_extra_config`):

- `load_skip_groups`: the group contributes an empty entry to load specs (workers already skip zero-size groups), so its short block table never trips the allocation assert;
- manager-level **always-hit / never-store** for those groups, so they neither gate nor pollute the hit window;
- `hit_rollback_tokens`: report one mamba-align segment (3,584 tokens here) fewer hit tokens, so the engine **recomputes** the trailing segment — which honestly rebuilds tail/conv/drafter state from the restored KV. Correctness verified by needle-in-context checks across 30/30 restore tests, including 10 simultaneous restores after a full engine restart.

Implementation is small (the scheduler hooks are ~30 lines; the manager policy lives in an out-of-tree spec): scheduler hunks in https://gist.github.com/hughmadden/dcada6409ae5a94e623f0ea9c3108de0 (sections 8–9), manager side in https://gist.github.com/hughmadden/03f369339b709a80fd594f4083702722.

Longer term this probably wants to be a `KVCacheSpec`-level attribute (e.g. `offloadable: bool`) with the rollback window derived automatically, rather than user config — happy to co-design or PR either shape.

Companion issue for the geometry half: #54413.

items.title: [Feature][KV-offloading]: OffloadingConnector rejects hybrid models whose KV groups have blocks smaller than one hash unit (GLM-5.3-Flash) — per-group blocks_per_chunk implementation attached
items.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

`build_offloading_config` asserts `tokens_per_block % tokens_per_hash == 0` for every KV cache group, so a hybrid model with any group whose blocks are *smaller* than a hash unit cannot enable the OffloadingConnector at all. GLM-5.3-Flash (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`, TP=2) is such a model — its DSA-indexer `tail_cache` group has **4-token blocks** under a 64-token hash grid. Boot-time group inventory from our deployment:

```
group[0]   UniformType 3584 tok  (MLA + indexer k_cache, 22 layers)
group[1]   UniformType    4 tok  (indexer tail_cache, 11 layers)   <- rejected
group[2-5] MambaSpec   3584 tok  (KDA state, align mode)
group[6]   UniformType   64 tok  (DFlash2 drafter)
tokens_per_hash = 64
```

This is the same disease family as #48635 (block_size uniformity, completed) and #48919 (eagle-group block-size mismatch, open): group geometry threaded through the stack as a single global scalar. #38261 attacks the same problem with a planner that splits groups, and #44865 reshapes transfer descriptors per-group — this issue offers a third, minimal-footprint approach plus a production data point, in the hope of converging on one design.

### Proposed change (running in production)

Support the divisor direction: a group with `tokens_per_hash % tokens_per_block == 0` aggregates `tokens_per_hash // tokens_per_block` GPU blocks per offloaded chunk. Concretely, `blocks_per_chunk` becomes **per-group** — derived on `OffloadingSpec`, carried on `GroupOffloadConfig`, and substituted at the scheduler sites that read the global scalar (`storable_chunks`, `update_state_after_alloc`, `_update_req_states`, `_build_store_jobs`, `resolve_mamba_align_size`, the `from_spec` geometry). `GPULoadStoreSpec.block_indices` already anticipates offload-units larger than GPU blocks.

One practical note: keeping the CPU staging tier **row-granular** (worker at bpc=1, manager allocating `bpc[g]` rows per key) sidesteps tensors shared between groups of different bpc — which this model has (`tail_cache` shares tensors with `k_cache`).

Patch (~150 lines, exact-string hunks against our deployed snapshot, straightforwardly portable): https://gist.github.com/hughmadden/dcada6409ae5a94e623f0ea9c3108de0

With this (plus a companion issue on recent-window group exclusion, filed separately) GLM-5.3-Flash + DFlash2 disk park/resume works end-to-end on 2× DGX Spark (GB10) TP=2: a 155k-token session restores in 36.6 s vs 205 s recompute, needle-correct; 30/30 correct under a 10-agent concurrency test. Happy to shape this into a PR or fold the idea into #38261/#44865 — whichever direction maintainers prefer.

### Alternatives

- #38261's HybridOffloadPlanner (group splitting) — heavier but more general.
- Excluding unaligned groups — insufficient alone: naive filtering corrupts positional group-index correspondence (`resolve_mamba_align_size` etc.), and some unaligned groups are genuinely restorable.

### Additional context

Found while building a node-local disk KV tier for a 2-node DGX Spark deployment; assert chain and follow-on findings documented in the gist header.

items.title: [Bug]: PD-admitted Mamba request is spec-padded before prefill completes, then align split truncates the 8-token window to 5
items.body:
## Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment and topology</summary>

```text
vLLM: v0.27.1, tag commit 6e448d0ea9bf3d88d898b65449ca6dc2aec170ac
Relevant merged change: #51113
  release commit: 3f9fc83067cdd377c51d58ad949380a164bee260
  upstream commit: c56f169d9ae46ca420617e2cf5f0c9135da0f651

Backend: vLLM Ascend, source installation from main plus Kimi-K3 support
Python: 3.11.10
Device: Ascend NPU
Engine: V1 with async scheduling

Deployment:
  - disaggregated prefill/decode using MooncakeConnectorV1
  - 2 prefill instances and 2 decode instances
  - each instance: TP=16
  - each P/D group: DP=2, one local DP rank per node
  - enable_prefix_caching=true
  - mamba_cache_mode=align on both P and D
  - Mamba/scheduler block size=384
  - max_model_len=133120
  - max_num_batched_tokens=8192
  - max_num_seqs=16
  - speculative method=DSpark, K=7, parallel draft TP=16

Model: Kimi-K3 hybrid attention/Mamba target with a compatible DSpark draft model.
For this scheduling/metadata investigation only, the target was loaded in a
10/93-layer reduced debug mode. This makes generated text unsuitable for model
quality evaluation, but does not change the scheduler transition described
below: prompt length, external-computed-token count, Mamba block split,
scheduled token count, or speculative placeholder count.

The same scheduler ordering is still present on vLLM main at
1ebff996a118cdc6e831c521c839d29ffe47d30f (checked 2026-08-30).
```

The full `collect_env.py` output is not attached because the reproduction ran
on an isolated multi-node environment. The values above are taken from the
startup and engine logs. Private host addresses, model paths, engine IDs and
request IDs have been removed.

</details>

## Describe the bug

### Summary

On a PD decode worker, a newly admitted request may have all but the last prompt
token supplied by the KV connector. If running decode requests are already in
the batch, the waiting-request scheduling path treats the one remaining token
as a new decode and pads it from 1 token to `1 + K` tokens.

For a hybrid Mamba model in `mamba_cache_mode="align"`, #51113 correctly clips
a prefill-like span that starts mid-block so it cannot cross the next Mamba
boundary. In our case the padded 8-token span starts at 379 and is clipped at
384, leaving only 5 physical query tokens. However, `pad_spec_decode` remains
true and the scheduler still publishes 7 speculative placeholders.

This creates a request-local contract violation:

```text
logical speculative window: 1 target + 7 drafts = 8
physical target span after Mamba split:          5
speculative placeholders/rejection window:      7
```

The global flattened batch shapes remain valid. The failure occurs when the
proposer interprets the 5-token request row using a 7-token rejection window.
On the Ascend DSpark backend this produces an invalid request-local position and
slot mapping and terminates the engine.

This is not a request to revert #51113. Its Mamba boundary protection is
required to prevent recurrent-state cache poisoning. The missing invariant is
that a synthetically padded speculative window must either survive all later
scheduler limiters atomically, or the padding must be cancelled for that
request.

### Deployment/startup configuration

The actual deployment uses a small wrapper to start one local DP rank on each
node. The following is a sanitized equivalent of the startup strategy:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

ROLE="$1"       # producer or consumer
DP_RANK="$2"    # 0 or 1 within the P group / D group
DP_ADDR="$3"    # shared coordinator address for that group
KV_PORT="$4"

export VLLM_USE_V1=1
export VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_MLAPO=1

SPEC_CONFIG='{
  "method": "dspark",
  "model": "<compatible-dspark-model>",
  "num_speculative_tokens": 7,
  "draft_tensor_parallel_size": 16,
  "max_model_len": 4096,
  "draft_sample_method": "greedy",
  "enforce_eager": true
}'

KV_CONFIG="{
  \"kv_connector\": \"MooncakeConnectorV1\",
  \"kv_role\": \"kv_${ROLE}\",
  \"kv_buffer_device\": \"npu\",
  \"kv_port\": ${KV_PORT},
  \"kv_connector_extra_config\": {
    \"prefill\": {\"dp_size\": 2, \"tp_size\": 16},
    \"decode\": {\"dp_size\": 2, \"tp_size\": 16}
  }
}"

vllm serve <kimi-k3-target-model> \
  --served-model-name kimi-k3 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 16 \
  --data-parallel-size 2 \
  --data-parallel-rank "${DP_RANK}" \
  --data-parallel-address "${DP_ADDR}" \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --max-model-len 133120 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --speculative-config "${SPEC_CONFIG}" \
  --kv-transfer-config "${KV_CONFIG}"
```

The Ascend platform selects `mamba_cache_mode=align` when prefix caching is
enabled and resolves the common scheduler/Mamba block size to 384. P and D use
the same cache mode and logical KV-manager group topology.

### Trigger conditions

All of the following are needed for the observed frame:

1. A hybrid Mamba/GDN model with `mamba_cache_mode=align`.
2. Speculative decoding with a fixed `K` (`K=7` here).
3. A PD consumer request admitted with an unaligned external prefix. In the
   failing request, `num_prompt_tokens=380` and the D scheduler starts from
   `num_computed_tokens=379`.
4. At least one normal decode request is already scheduled in the same step,
   while no other prefill has yet been scheduled. This satisfies the
   waiting-request `pad_spec_decode` condition.
5. Padding creates an interval that crosses the next Mamba boundary:
   `[379, 379 + 1 + 7) = [379, 387)` crosses 384.
6. `_mamba_block_aligned_split()` clips the physical interval to `[379,384)`,
   but the scheduler retains 7 speculative placeholders.
7. The proposer subsequently applies the full 7-token rejection/proposal
   semantics to this 5-token request row.

A single 380-token request normally does **not** reproduce the failure. It first
schedules the one remaining prompt token alone and enters ordinary decode in
the next step. The mixed running-decode/new-PD-request batch is important.

### Workload used to trigger the mixed batch

The original fatal frame was observed during a concurrent GPQA workload. We
then reduced the traffic pattern to the following controlled case:

1. Use `/tokenize` to construct a prompt with exactly 380 tokens.
2. Start four long-running decode requests (`temperature=0`,
   `max_tokens=768`) so both D schedulers have running decode rows.
3. Wait two seconds.
4. Concurrently submit twelve identical 380-token completion requests through
   the 2P+2D proxy.

Sanitized client outline:

```bash
# Keep decode batches active.
for i in $(seq 1 4); do
  curl -sS -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{
      "model":"kimi-k3",
      "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<long deterministic request>"}],
      "temperature":0,
      "max_tokens":768,
      "stream":false
    }' \
    http://<pd-proxy>/v1/chat/completions >"runner_${i}.json" &
done

sleep 2

# The prompt in exact_380.json was verified by /tokenize to contain 380 tokens.
for i in $(seq 1 12); do
  curl -sS -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --data-binary @exact_380.json \
    http://<pd-proxy>/v1/completions >"exact_380_${i}.json" &
done
wait
```

`exact_380.json`:

```json
{
  "model": "kimi-k3",
  "prompt": "<neutral repeated text tokenized to exactly 380 tokens>",
  "temperature": 0,
  "max_tokens": 16,
  "stream": false
}
```

The controlled workload deterministically reaches the same scheduler state on
both D instances (`start=379, requested=8, result=5, end=384`). The fatal
unpatched metadata frame quoted below comes from the original concurrent GPQA
run; the controlled workload was also used for subsequent isolation and fix
validation.

### Exact scheduler transition

The relevant waiting-request path currently behaves as follows:

```text
request.num_prompt_tokens = 380
num_computed_tokens        = 379  # external PD prefix ends here
real remaining prompt      = 1
num_spec_tokens            = 7

padding before split:
  num_new_tokens = 1 + 7 = 8
  pad_spec_decode = true

Mamba align split (#51113):
  start               = 379
  next_block_boundary = 384
  requested           = 8
  returned            = 384 - 379 = 5

scheduler output:
  num_scheduled_tokens[request]          = 5
  scheduled_spec_decode_tokens[request] = [-1] * 7
```

The ordering is visible in `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`: the waiting path
sets `pad_spec_decode`, `_mamba_block_aligned_split()` is called later, and the
placeholder list is populated after slot allocation without checking whether
the padded width survived.

### Observed result

The failing batch contained 12 requests:

```text
num_scheduled_tokens = [5, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8, 8]
total_num_scheduled_tokens = 93 = 5 + 11 * 8
query_start_loc.shape = [13]
input_ids.shape = [93]
```

Therefore the batch-level shapes are internally consistent. Only request row 0
is semantically invalid:

```text
prompt_tokens     = 380
computed_tokens   = 379
scheduled_tokens  = 5
num_ctx           = 5
seq_len           = 384
num_rejected      = 7
valid_ctx_end     = 5 - 7 = -2

expected query positions = [377, 378, 379, 380, 381, 382, 383]
actual query positions   = [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]
actual query slots       = [-1, -1, -1, -1, -1, -1, -1]
metadata_valid           = false
```

The first fatal error is:

```text
RuntimeError: Invalid DSpark input metadata; see DSPARK_METADATA_MISMATCH
for request index 0, kv-cache group 0.

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py", line 1010, in worker_busy_loop
    output = func(*args, **kwargs)
  File "vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py", line 714, in sample_tokens
    return self.model_runner.sample_tokens(grammar_output)
  File "vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py", line 2380, in sample_tokens
    propose_draft_token_ids(sampler_output.sampled_token_ids)
  File "vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py", line 1708, in propose_draft_token_ids
    draft_token_ids = self.drafter._propose(...)
  File "vllm_ascend/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py", line 827, in _propose
    ... = self.set_inputs_first_pass(...)
  File "vllm_ascend/spec_decode/dspark_proposer.py", line 541, in set_inputs_first_pass
    raise RuntimeError(...)
```

Without the diagnostic guard, the invalid position/slot mapping would proceed
toward the device kernel. The guard turns it into a deterministic host-side
failure instead of a possible device-side out-of-bounds access.

### Isolation and validation results

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Small end-to-end PD request | HTTP 200; Mooncake transfer succeeds |
| One exact 380-token request without active decode traffic | Schedules 1 prompt token, then normal 8-token decode; no 5-vs-7 frame |
| Concurrent GPQA, mixed new PD admissions and running decode rows | Reproduces fatal `scheduled=5`, `num_rejected=7`, `valid_ctx_end=-2` frame |
| Controlled 4 long runners + 12 exact-380 requests | Reaches `start=379, requested=8, result=5, end=384` on both D instances |
| Temporarily restore the pre-#51113 `next_boundary <= last_cache_position` predicate | No 384 split and no metadata error, but reintroduces the prefix-cache poisoning fixed by #51113; not an acceptable fix |
| Keep #51113 and cancel/degrade speculative processing for the short request row | All requests return HTTP 200; no invalid metadata; subsequent scheduling continues from 384 |
| Keep #51113 and rebuild the DSpark anchor from the valid accepted end | All requests return HTTP 200; no invalid metadata; normal rows in the same mixed batch remain speculative |

The last two experiments confirm that the 384 stop itself is valid and that the
failure is the stale logical speculative width after the physical span is
shortened. They are backend-side experiments, not proposed as the preferred
upstream fix.

### Expected behavior

The last uncached prompt token on a PD consumer should remain a prefill token.
It should be scheduled alone, and speculative decode should begin on a later
step after the request has crossed the prefill/decode phase boundary.

More generally, when a scheduler marks a request as synthetically padded for
speculative decode, the final physical width after all limiters must be exactly
the padded width. If a Mamba split, token budget, encoder cap, long-prefill cap,
or any later limiter shortens it, the scheduler must cancel the synthetic
padding and not emit `K` placeholders for the shortened row.

### Suspected scheduler fix

The minimal phase guard is the same distinction discussed in #49495: do not
classify `num_new_tokens == 1` as a new decode solely by token count. Require
that prompt prefill has actually completed:

```diff
 if (
     (self.num_spec_tokens > 0 and self.dynamic_sd_lookup is None)
     and self.num_sampled_tokens_per_step > 0
     and num_new_tokens == 1
+    and num_computed_tokens >= request.num_prompt_tokens
     and (scheduled_running_reqs and not prefill_scheduled)
 ):
```

For the failing PD request, `379 < 380`, so it would schedule the one real prompt
token and would not advertise seven draft placeholders.

A defensive invariant should also be considered after all token-count limiters:

```text
if pad_spec_decode and final_num_new_tokens != padded_num_tokens:
    cancel speculative padding for this request
    schedule only its real remaining token(s)
    do not populate scheduled_spec_decode_tokens for this row
```

This would protect against future limiters that can shorten a padded window,
not only Mamba alignment.

Suggested regression test:

```text
hybrid Mamba align scheduler, block_size=384, K=7
one running decode request
one waiting request with prompt_tokens=380
connector reports external_computed_tokens=379

expected:
  num_scheduled_tokens[new_request] == 1
  new_request not in scheduled_spec_decode_tokens

must not produce:
  num_scheduled_tokens[new_request] == 5
  len(scheduled_spec_decode_tokens[new_request]) == 7
```

It would also be useful to parameterize this test for generic MTP/EAGLE. The
scheduler condition and window atomicity are not DSpark-specific, although the
exact error manifestation is backend/proposer-dependent.

### Related issues and PRs

- #51113 — required Mamba align boundary correctness; this report describes an
  interaction exposed by that fix, not a reason to revert it.
- #49495 — another case where a one-token prefill remainder is mistaken for a
  new decode by the padded waiting-request optimization.
- #53505 — related hybrid Mamba + KV connector + speculative-decoding family,
  but it reports recurrent-state corruption through connector prefix-cache
  reconciliation rather than this 5-token/7-placeholder mismatch.

### Before submitting a new issue

- [x] Searched existing open and closed issues, including #49495 and #53505.
- [x] Removed private hosts, credentials, paths, engine IDs and request IDs from
  the report.

items.title: [Doc]: Document hybrid NIXL DS-layout requirement and connector HMA compatibility
items.body:
### 📚 The doc issue

We recently brought up 1P1D disaggregated serving for a hybrid model
(Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8, 3x Gated DeltaNet + 1x Gated Attention) with `NixlConnector` on a
single GB10 (unified-memory) machine. The feature works — this issue is only about how
hard the requirements are to find in the repo docs. Everything below was checked against
`main` on 2026-08-30.

**1. The DS-layout requirement appears nowhere under `docs/`.** The NixlConnector
compatibility matrix lists `Hybrid SSM / Mamba → Basic PD ✅`, and hybrid support is
tracked in #40017 with GDN transfer merged in #41869 — so hybrid disagg is documented as
supported. But actually launching it requires `VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS`: the
default conv-state layout is `SD`, and the NIXL hybrid worker asserts on it directly
("3-read Mamba conv transfer requires DS conv state layout. Set
VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS"). The variable is registered in `envs.py`, and a recent
official vLLM recipe explicitly sets it — but there are zero mentions under `docs/`: not
in `disagg_prefill.md`, the NixlConnector usage guide, or the compatibility matrix. In
practice one discovers it inside the repo by launching, failing, and reading the assert.

**2. Connector HMA compatibility is not visible in the docs.** Across connectors,
`NixlConnector` and `MooncakeConnector` declare the `SupportsHMA` capability contract,
while `MoRIIOConnector` and `LMCacheConnectorV1` currently do not (checked on main,
2026-08-30). Current vLLM disables HMA when the selected connector does not advertise HMA
support, and the config warning itself notes that hybrid SSM models require HMA and will
fail at startup without it. This capability distinction is not currently visible in the
disaggregated-prefill documentation. (We make no claim about end-to-end hybrid coverage
of any connector beyond the declared capability — that is precisely what a support note
per connector could clarify.)

**Related:** #49537 and #42620 track hybrid connector/runtime support (KV-transfer for
hybrid-attention models, including Mooncake behavior); #42882 proposes making DS the
default layout, which would remove the env-var requirement — until then it needs
documenting. This issue is specifically about documentation discoverability, not runtime
support.

Environment: vLLM main (source build) — hybrid 1P1D verified working end-to-end with
`VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS`; NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10 unified memory),
Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8.

AI-assisted investigation disclosure: environment archaeology and doc-search performed
with Claude Code under human direction; all claims re-verified against main by hand.

### Suggest a potential alternative/fix

- A sentence in the compatibility matrix's footnotes and/or the NixlConnector usage guide
  stating the `VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS` requirement for hybrid SSM/Mamba transfer —
  happy to send that docs PR.
- If welcome, a cross-connector "hybrid models" note in `disagg_prefill.md` (which
  connectors declare HMA support and what happens when one does not) — glad to draft it.

This is a sanitized, manually reconstructed host/container snapshot assembled from metadata-only checks of the tested image and both nodes. It is not presented as verbatim output from `collect_env.py` because repeating the full-model startup after a dual-GPU Xid was judged unsafe. The attached bundle contains `environment.json` with the same values and provenance caveat.

### Bug description

#### Summary

This is a one-shot evidence report, not a minimal runnable reproducer. The original run did not use `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG` or `VLLM_TRACE_FUNCTION=1`, and I did not repeat an unchanged startup after simultaneous GPU Xids solely to collect those diagnostics.

A two-node DeepSeek V4 + DSpark K=5 startup progressed through TP=2 initialization, model loading, KV profiling, and FlashInfer sparse-MLA autotuning, but failed before API readiness during PIECEWISE CUDA-graph warmup.

Both GB10 GPUs reported Xid 31 MMU virtual-write faults at the same wall-clock second. Rank 1's closest Python stack traversed the DeepSeek V4 attention path into FlashInfer's DSv4 SM120/SM121 sparse-MLA runner. CUDA explicitly warned that the error may have been reported asynchronously, so this stack identifies where the poisoned context surfaced, not necessarily the kernel that caused the write.

The failing graph size is inferred to be T=16: capture uses descending sizes; 36, 32, 30, and 24 completed (4/9) before the next pre-capture forward failed. T=16 was not directly instrumented in this run.

#### Expected behavior

PIECEWISE CUDA-graph warmup completes and the TP=2 API becomes ready.

#### Observed behavior

- TP=2/NCCL formed successfully.
- Target weights loaded successfully; the K=5 draft then loaded all 97 draft parameters. Total model loading reached about 79.48 GiB per rank.
- KV profiling completed.
- FlashInfer sparse-MLA autotuning loaded 24 cached configurations.
- PIECEWISE warmup reached 4/9 capture sizes.
- Both GPUs emitted Xid 31 `ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_WRITE` faults at 2026-08-29 06:34:18 UTC.
- Rank 0 surfaced `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` at a later FP8 allocation.
- Rank 1 surfaced `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` while constructing `_SparseMLAPagedAttentionRunner` after the stack passed through `flashinfer_sparse.py:857`.
- Rank 1 later emitted Xid 13 ×16 and Xid 109 ×1. TCPStore/NCCL errors occurred after rank 0 died and are treated as secondary fallout.
- The API never became ready. No correctness, throughput, or soak result exists.

The kernel journals also contained driver-level `NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY` allocation probes before the fault (135 on rank 0 and 42 on rank 1). These may be a pressure cofactor. There was no PyTorch OOM, Docker OOM kill, or container restart.

#### Why this appears distinct from existing reports

- #50720 remains open and covers a deterministic `num_tokens > 64` assertion caused by short-token DSpark routing. That failure class was separately cleared in a local v0.27.1 test by patching both source and the active precompiled FlashInfer module; TP=2 then reached readiness without Xid: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/50720#issuecomment-5385709649
- The tested tree includes the exact #52499 head (`af2456b11328a15ea7f2f8e48aeb7ed30a61e32f`), covering flat 3-D speculative-decode queries and ≤64-token routing.
- The tested tree ports both changes from #53425 head (`ed71de505898e1c006de15958795c229c9f7e21f`) onto v0.28, covering SM12x FlashInfer kernel page size 64.
- vLLM 0.28.0 already includes #51538's DSpark CUDA-graph workspace-lifetime, graph-replay, and draft-KV-write safeguards. This failure persisted despite those adjacent protections.
- #53391 is the closest GB10 startup report: DSV4 + DSpark + TP=2 on two GB10s. It is a deterministic `ragged spec decode batch: 7 tokens over 2 requests` assertion during kernel warmup; this tested tree includes its separate query-offset-driven ragged-dispatch port and instead reaches graph capture before a GPU fault.
- #51499 and #51970 report DeepSeek V4 CUDA illegal-memory failures from all-zero indexer lengths reaching an out-of-bounds DeepGEMM paged-MQA metadata scheduler on H20/GH200. Their localized path and capture shapes differ from this two-GB10, PIECEWISE, inferred-T=16 sparse-MLA-adjacent observation. Because this run lacked synchronous launch localization, it does not rule out an earlier asynchronous fault in another path.
- FlashInfer #4802 head (`c2eec117219457e45126fa4fa87e7240dd4ea620`) directly refactors the same SM120 T≤64 sparse-MLA/CUDA-graph surface. It adds a persistent graph-safe runner and documents a lazy-allocation/free graph-memory-pool reuse hazard. This candidate did not include #4802, and its description does not diagnose this dual-rank Xid 31. I can validate a maintainer-specified #4802-head build if that is the preferred next check.

I searched open and closed vLLM issues for DeepSeek V4/DSpark + SM121/GB10 + TP=2 + T=16 + Xid 31 and did not find an equivalent report. The closest neighboring reports are distinguished above; #50189 and #53455 involve materially different models, execution paths, or configurations.

#### Exact source provenance

This was not stock vLLM 0.28.0 or stock FlashInfer 0.6.16.post3.

vLLM:

- Base tag/commit: `v0.28.0` / `2cf0a6915ce544dc493a0990f2ea38d81601128a`
- Tested local commit/tree: `9165323e2ebffbb0260d7df9feb955b87330f83b` / `7637f703bd2d9e94bb6a8f6516ef5ba7bb69685d`
- Included #52368, #52018, exact #52499 head, exact #53425 head, validated SM12x sparse-indexer fallbacks, contiguous/ragged speculative-decode fixes, and public SM12x Triton O-projection commit `409086a5f588d155ffbddd4bb7b917c96333ed3c`.

FlashInfer:

- Base tag/commit: `v0.6.16.post3` / `9dc1b2495b40314dec8a8cde8cd7faf5c5206702`
- Tested local commit/tree: `1fb01df312cefb0eaea004fd4c7e513848eb3952` / `62ef2a19f1b8ea4f21392eb9ae7d60d786c8f76e`
- Included the DeepSeek V4 H32/K192 support from #4380 and the narrow SM120/SM121 prefill-handshake fix associated with #4732.

The local replay commits are not publicly fetchable. The attached bundle therefore includes consolidated patches against the two stated base commits plus `source-lock.json`.

#### Launch configuration

Key observed vLLM settings were:

- tensor parallel size 2 across two nodes
- pipeline parallel size 1
- DSpark with five speculative tokens, probabilistic sampling, adaptive verification disabled
- FP8 KV cache
- block size 256
- maximum model length 532,288
- GPU memory utilization 0.810
- maximum sequences 6
- maximum batched tokens 8,192
- long-prefill threshold 1,024
- chunked prefill and async scheduling enabled
- FlashInfer autotuning enabled
- B12X linear and MoE backends
- PIECEWISE capture sizes `[1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 24, 30, 32, 36]`

The bundle's `launch-observed.yaml` records a sanitized subset of the observed launch and container configuration. It is evidence, not a cutover script or minimized reproducer.

#### Primary error excerpts

Rank 1:

```text
compile_or_warm_up_model
  -> capture_model
  -> cudagraph_utils.py:337 forward_fn(CUDAGraphMode.NONE)
  -> deepseek_v4/attention.py
  -> flashinfer_sparse.py:857 _forward_decode
  -> flashinfer.mla._core._trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4_sm120
  -> _SparseMLAPagedAttentionRunner(...)
  -> torch.empty(...)
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
CUDA kernel errors might be asynchronously reported at some other API call,
so the stacktrace below might be incorrect.
```

Kernel evidence, with hostnames, PCI addresses, process identifiers, GPU UUIDs, channels, and virtual addresses removed:

```text
2026-08-29T06:34:18Z rank0 NVRM: Xid 31, MMU Fault, FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_WRITE
2026-08-29T06:34:18Z rank1 NVRM: Xid 31, MMU Fault, FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_WRITE
2026-08-29T06:34:18Z rank1 NVRM: Xid 31, MMU Fault, FAULT_PTE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_WRITE
```

Sanitized rank excerpts and the compact kernel fault window are included in `logs/`.

#### Negative controls

The standalone controls did not reproduce the fault:

- The prior SM121 O-projection blocker passed eager execution plus CUDA-graph capture/replay at T=10, 96, and 8,192 on both nodes.
- Standalone FlashInfer sparse MLA at T=16, H=32, D=512, K=192 passed the heuristic and explicit tactics 1, 2, and 3.
- Corrected cached-shape tests passed K128/tactic 2, K128+512/tactic 8, and a 4,224-wide K128 buffer with 4,158 valid compressed entries/tactic 52, using eager/reference checks and alternating A/B/A/B graph replays.
- No Xid, illegal-memory event, OOM kill, or restart occurred in those controls.

The full-model warmup's exact T=16 metadata was not captured or reproduced. These controls also do not recreate full TP=2 allocation pressure, production tensor strides/buffer reuse, or stream ordering. They rule out a simple always-failing T=16 kernel/tactic explanation.

#### Reproduction status and limitations

- The full-model failure was observed once in one attended startup and was not repeated because it produced simultaneous GPU Xids.
- T=16 is inferred from capture order, not directly instrumented.
- Rank 1's sparse-MLA stack is the closest report, not proof of causation.
- Memory pressure may contribute, but this was not a framework/container OOM.
- The exact model is publicly listed but gated; no weights or cache content are in the bundle.
- `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG` and `VLLM_TRACE_FUNCTION=1` were not used in the original one-time failure. Repeating the same startup solely to collect them was judged unsafe.

#### Evidence bundle

The proposed compact source-and-evidence bundle is available at:

https://github.com/TurboTheTurtle/vllm-gb10-dsv4-xid31-evidence
